style.label: Tone and terminology
style.hint: — not sure? leave both on Auto
style.speechKoreanOnly: Choosing sentence endings is a Korean-specific decision, so it is not used for {{lang}}. Switch the target language back to Korean to pick one.
style.speechHint_auto: Decided per surface: polite for UI, whatever fits for NPC lines. One character's register never drifts mid-conversation, whichever option you pick.
style.speechHint_polite: One polite register across the whole pack — "…합니다", "…하세요". NPC chatter and flavour text included, no exceptions.
style.speechHint_banmal: One casual register across the whole pack — "…해", "…야", "…지". Suits packs with a friendly, informal voice.
style.speechHint_hage: The archaic familiar register throughout — "…하네", "…인가?", "자네". Makes medieval and high-fantasy packs like Prominence read far more in character.
style.termHint_auto: Terms with no established Korean name are handled as they are today — translated when the meaning is clear, sounded out when the word is invented.
style.termHint_translate: With no established name, render the meaning: Sunfire Blade → 태양불꽃 검. Glossary rules and official names still win.
style.termHint_transliterate: With no established name, sound it out: Sunfire Blade → 선파이어 블레이드. Glossary rules and official names still win.
